Maya Thompson: Quick heads-up  new Dependent Travel guidance goes live 2026-05-01. Short version below, full addendum on the intranet: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/dependent-travel

Diego Ramos: What counts as a dependent?

Maya Thompson: Children under 13, elderly dependents in your household, or dependents with documented care needs. Just a one-line statement in the expense is fine.

Nia Carter: Key points: 1) Up to $500 per qualifying trip (per-trip cap). 2) Annual max $1,000 per employee, use-it-or-lose-it by calendar year. 3) Emergency bridge support up to $200/day for 3 days. 4) Eligible: FT and PT >=0.6 FTE; contractors excluded (exception review possible).

Owen Li: Submit where?

Maya Thompson: Use Expensify for DEP-TRAV (were rolling it there for faster approvals). Attach receipts and a one-line justification tying it to the business trip.

Samir (Legal): Tax note: US claims under $1k/yr are generally non-taxable for bona fide business-related dependent care tied to travel. Non-US tax treatment varies  include your payroll region in the note if outside the US.

Diego Ramos: Are visa fees covered?

Maya Thompson: Visa/immigration costs are excluded unless pre-approved for mission-critical travel. Contact people-ops@redwood.com before you book.
